title: Apply a matrix change set through slicer relay-roles apply
lead: *Proposed.* A daemon method `matrix.apply` and the command `ork roles matrix apply PROJECT (--file PATH | --stdin) [--dry-run] [--json]` pass a JSON change set to `slicer relay-roles apply` in the registered project and return slicer's result, plus ork's warning for each row whose agent has no ork adapter. A dry run returns slicer's validated result and writes nothing. The set is either a list of edit steps (`ops`) or a complete matrix (`replace`). It needs slicer's `relay-roles apply` (slicer outline `relay-roles-apply`) and, for `replace`, its second item `relay-roles-replace`.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner, 2026-11-02: set up the role matrix per project from ork, UI first, and also from the CLI and AI-driven workflows; slicer keeps the matrix. S173 (wire half of the matrix editor) runs one `relay-roles` verb per call, and its preview is ork's argv, not slicer's verdict (S173 Why: `matrix.edit` with `preview` returns the `command` without running anything). A change of several rows (the 2026-11-02 Grok rows r21-r24 took four `relay-roles add` calls) is not atomic and cannot be checked as a whole before it runs. slicer's `relay-roles apply` (*proposed*) takes the set, checks every step, guards with `expect` against a stale read, and saves once.

This slice does not replace S173 or S226: they stay unchanged in v1.1 on slicer 1.18, and this slice is v1.2 (owner, 2026-11-02, interactive). The owner also reversed the 2026-10-29 "TUI only" answer on 2026-11-02: ork gets a CLI form, which is this slice's `ork roles matrix apply`. The owner chose on 2026-11-02 that the apply form also takes a whole matrix (`replace`).

Boundary: the matrix is slicer's (`docs/boundaries.md:14`, `lineup.source`); ork passes the set through and never edits `.slicer/relay-roles.json`.

Wire (*proposed*): `matrix.apply {project, set, dry_run?}`, where `set` is the object slicer reads (`{"expect"?, "ops": [...]}` or `{"expect"?, "replace": {"rows": [...], "rules": [...]}}`), passed to slicer unchanged on stdin. ork checks only that `set` is a JSON object with exactly one of `ops` and `replace`; slicer validates the rest. Result: slicer's `--json` result unchanged under `slicer`, plus `warnings: ["r25: agent \"Acme\" has no ork adapter: a plan skips this row", ...]` for each row in the result whose agent is not in `matrixAdapters` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:336-337`, lower-cased) and that slicer's `steps` list as an `add` or `set` with `changed: true` (for `replace` too, since slicer reports its derived steps). slicer's error (code and message) comes back verbatim, including `stale_revision`. A slicer without the command (argparse `invalid choice`, exit 2) is reported as `slicer_too_old: slicer relay-roles apply is not available in this slicer; upgrade slicer (ork doctor --upgrade)`. A slicer that has `apply` but not `replace` refuses the key with its own `usage` error, which comes back verbatim. The write lands in the main checkout and stays uncommitted (owner, 2026-10-29).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestRelayRolesApplyArgvAndStdin` (`internal/slicercli`): the call is exactly `relay-roles apply --stdin --render --json --root ROOT` with the set bytes on stdin; `--dry-run` adds `--dry-run` and drops `--render`. Fails first: no function.
- `TestMatrixApplyPassesTheSetAndReturnsSlicersResult` (`internal/daemon`): the result's `slicer` part equals the fake's stdout byte for byte (as JSON). Fails first: unknown method.
- `TestMatrixApplyDryRunWritesNothingAndStillWarns`: a dry-run set that adds an `Acme` row returns the `warnings` line for it.
- `TestMatrixApplyWarnsOnlyForAddedOrChangedRows`: an existing Grok row that the set does not touch gives no warning.
- `TestMatrixApplyPassesSlicersRefusalThrough`: `stale_revision`, `unknown_role_row` and `bad_role_field` come back with code and message unchanged; no run record.
- `TestMatrixApplyOnAnOldSlicer`: argparse's `invalid choice: 'apply'` (exit 2) becomes `slicer_too_old`.
- `TestMatrixApplyPassesAReplaceUnchanged`: a `replace` set reaches slicer's stdin byte for byte, and an `Acme` row that slicer's `steps` report as added gets a warning.
- `TestMatrixApplyReplaceOnASlicerWithoutReplace`: slicer's `usage` refusal of the `replace` key comes back with code and message unchanged.
- `TestMatrixApplyRefusesBadRequests`: missing project, unknown project, a `set` that is not a JSON object, has neither `ops` nor `replace`, or has both: `bad_params` or `not_found`, no call.
- `TestMatrixApplyOverTheSocket`.
- CLI: `TestRolesMatrixApplyReadsTheFileOrStdin` (an `ops` file and a `replace` file), `TestRolesMatrixApplyDryRunText` (one line per step and the warnings), `TestRolesMatrixApplyJSONIsTheWireResult`, `TestRolesMatrixApplyUsage` (both or neither of `--file` and `--stdin`).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Do not start before slicer's `relay-roles apply` and its `replace` form are released and installed (`slicer --version`); doctor's minimum slicer version is not raised by this slice.
2. Write the failing tests; see each fail for the reason given.
3. Client, handler (resolve with `d.registered`; zero `runrec.Writer{}` as `itemNote`), warnings from `matrixAdapters`, wire, client call.
4. CLI `ork roles matrix apply` (owner, 2026-11-02).
5. Docs; CHANGELOG last.
6. Do not touch `internal/tui`, `internal/daemon/runs.go` (read `matrixAdapters` only), S173's `matrix.edit`, or the matrix of this repository.

UI slice: UI pass (r14).
